method.label: Use a polynomial for squared tangents

annotationRationale: Complex eighth powers and the binomial theorem produce the polynomial. Comparing its coefficients yields the pairwise products, and complementary-angle identities identify the two products to subtract.
sourceMethod: Followed the official complex eighth-power expansion and coefficient comparison. Rewrote the even degree-eight polynomial as a quartic in squared tangents, then removed the two complementary-angle products.

review.mathCheck: Taking real parts of the eighth power gives the quartic u^4−28u^3+70u^2−28u+1. Its four squared-tangent roots are distinct because the angles are acute and tangent increases there. Their six pairwise products sum to 70; the two omitted complementary pairs each contribute 1. The result is 68, choice B.
review.sourceMethodCheck: Faithful, originally worded adaptation of MAA solution 23, page 16: complex eighth powers, coefficient comparison, then complementary-pair subtraction. Passing directly to squared tangents is equivalent to the official even polynomial.
review.annotationCheck: All selected concepts are used. Division by the cosine, distinctness of roots, coefficient signs, and the two omitted terms are justified. The explanation is reconstructible at AMC 12 level.
